source_refs.note: Topic 30.7 (PDF 212). The CDCl3 13C signal printed 'near 80 ppm' is given with its usual value, about 77 ppm.

blocks.text: The 12C nucleus has no magnetic properties, because it has even numbers of protons and neutrons, so it is NMR inactive. The 13C nucleus has a magnetic spin because of its odd number of neutrons, so 13C NMR spectra can be recorded for carbon compounds. As in 1H NMR, the chemical shift (delta, in ppm) is measured from TMS at 0.0 ppm, but the 13C range is 0-220 ppm. Deuterated chloroform, CDCl3, is usually the solvent; it gives a small signal of its own (the book says near 80 ppm; it is at about 77 ppm).

blocks.prompt: Why does 12C give no NMR signal while 13C does?
blocks.explanation: 12C has even numbers of protons and neutrons, so it has no nuclear spin; 13C has an odd number of neutrons and so has a spin.

items: 13C is NMR active (odd neutrons); 12C is not.
13C shifts span 0-220 ppm from TMS; CDCl3 is the usual solvent.
